items.title: Houston Person Part 1 interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Majesty of the Seas, May 29, 1995…

ctx.x: I was going to ask you that, because you know I’m of the opinion, and I just want to get a thought from you on this. I’m of the opinion that I don’t think if the person who planted that bomb, the same morning he did that, had sat down and listened to a Mozart symphony or a good album side by Ellington, I don’t think he could have put that bomb there.

That’s what I was talking about, getting everybody computer literate with no compassion. Cause there’s no art. I went to a movie, I saw a movie, Martin Sheen was in it, I don’t remember what it was, but it was about he was making a statement about teachers. And one teacher liking Shakespeare and Mozart, and Martin Sheen answers, say, “well I’m not worried about him ‘cause as long as he does that he’ll have compassion.” You know he was talking about the science, of this guy who was in science, but he still…

compassionate.” See and as long as we have balanced individuals and a balanced approach to life and education, I mean it still requires our science and math students to study art, then there will always be compassion around, and nobody will get overboard in one thing in a so-called specialized society where we have people who just do this, that’s all they do. You know like somebody’s attempt to stay like with a computer like 12 or 14 hours, and really just have a ball man. There’s something wrong with that.…
